title: Abolishment
paragraphs: “Now then, speak. What happened to Shieldfreeden’s Seven Star Hero? Hmm?”
“B-Buhi…”

When the Pig King asked, one of Takt’s pig followers groaned, as if reluctant to answer. Hahaha, committing crimes never pays. If you can’t even put your deeds into words, it means you’ve drowned yourself in wrongdoing. By the way, I can tell Father everything without hiding a thing. Though, I do get scolded afterward.

“For someone who claims to be Shieldfreeden’s representative, what does it say about you that you’re conspiring with the criminal Takt? How do you think the citizens of Shieldfreeden will react when they learn the truth?”

The Pig King spoke in a mocking tone. Indeed, the people of Shieldfreeden would never imagine that their own hero had already been killed. Let alone that their national representative had aided in the crime. If this were to come to light, it would surely cause turmoil—just as it did in the current Melromarc.

“A representative of your standing, conspiring with a criminal who attempted to overthrow my kingdom… And including the murder of your own Seven Star Hero—should we take this as Shieldfreeden’s official stance?”
“Bu…”
The pig—presumably Shieldfreeden’s representative—glared at the Pig King with hatred. Why do cornered swines always look so repulsive?
“Buhuhuhu… Well then, we shall immediately confirm this matter with Shieldfreeden. By royal decree of Faubrey, no less.”

This time, they couldn’t spread false information like they had before. After all, the King of Faubrey himself, along with knights and soldiers, stood witness. And the Seven Star Weapon—proof itself—was right before their eyes.
“B-Buhihihihi!”
As Takt’s pigs began to panic, Father and the others readied for battle. It seems these fools intend to settle things by force.
“Do they even have a chance of winning?” Itsuki replied with exasperation.
They likely realized things weren’t going their way and decided to forcefully rescue Takt.
“I’ll make sure Ren and I prevent them from escaping. Motoyasu, Father, I leave the rest to you.”
If they escape, it’ll be a major hassle. That’s precisely why we made all these preparations.
“You talk as if this is some great injustice, but by world standards, Takt is a high-profile criminal. Not that I expect you to listen…”

“Takt, a criminal? No! Takt is the treasure of this world! He will soon become the god who saves everything! Takt can do no wrong… No, Takt is the law! And for lowly interlopers like you to stand in his way is an offense worthy of death!”
What an utterly selfish statement. Then allow me to respond in kind.
“Takt, save the world? Impossible.”
“What!?”

That’s right. Takt is nothing more than a festering wound upon this world—he can’t even properly wield the Seven Star Weapons. Does he even realize how many people have suffered because of him? And judging from this dragon’s behavior… I tightened my grip on my spear.
“Someone who murdered at least two Heroes can never be considered a Hero himself. And even after hiding that crime, he’s still covering up countless other truths—despite the world being in crisis.”
“Indeed, someone like that cannot go unpunished.”
“Buhuhuhu… The Four Holy Heroes speak the truth. Takt has no cause worth defending. You may as well surrender now.”
Even after that declaration, Takt’s pigs still chose to resort to violence.
“As one who inherits the fragments of the Emperor Dragon, I declare—”
Rival flapped its wings and pointed at Takt’s dragon. But its voice… was no longer Rival’s. It was the voice of the parent.

“A being who slaughters Filolials in such a cowardly manner, driven only by instinct, has no right to the title of Dragon Emperor! The Dragon Emperor is the king of monsters, and a king must uphold the dignity of their status!”
“Hah! You insignificant fragment, don’t make me laugh! I’ll slaughter you Four Heroes and those pigs right here and now!”
“Booo!”
All of them rushed forward at once. It seems they really think they can win. Well, I recall hearing that their levels were around 250, so their confidence is likely misplaced arrogance.
“Motoyasu!”
“Uh, make sure not to kill anyone except our designated targets. That’s… what we were asked to do, after all.”
Father glanced briefly at the Pig King. That’s right. This was necessary to build a better relationship going forward.
“I understand! Aiming Lancer X!”
I unleashed Aiming Lancer, turning all of the charging pigs into pincushions.
“Boo!?”
“Grh… I’m not done yet!”
Takt’s dragon, along with his griffin, charged at us in retaliation. It’s big, so it must be tough. The real hassle is making sure we hold back enough to only inflict status ailments.
“Gyaooooooo!!”
“Air Strike Shield… X!”

Father instantly summoned a shield, placing it before us like a protective wall. Takt’s dragon roared as it swung its claws, enhanced with magic, in an attempt to shatter it. It looked like it planned to crush both the shield and us in a single attack. However, with a resounding clang , its claws slammed into the shield—followed immediately by its face colliding with it.
“What!? My level is—”
“Don’t underestimate the Four Holy Heroes!”
“Indeed. If you think you can defeat us with that , you’re sorely mistaken.”
“Then allow me to finish this! This is for injuring Sakura-chan! Gungnir X!”
I recalled how some fantasy-obsessed pig once said that dragons have a weakness in their foreheads. Though, honestly, any creature would die if you pierced them through the forehead.
“Guah—!”
My thrown Gungnir spear struck true, piercing straight through Takt’s dragon’s head. With a loud crash, the dragon collapsed, scattering blood across the battlefield.
“Damn it! I swear on my life, I will destroy you so-called ‘heroes’ who dare to protect the Filolials—”
“You’re just as guilty! Meteor Spear X!”
“Wha!? Ugh, Takt, hel—”

I took down the griffin as well, just for good measure. Oh? My spear is still reacting, as if demanding to pierce another target. It’s pointing toward empty space… The icon appearing is for the Beast Spear. Which means… there’s a fox hiding there!
“Hiding is pointless! Burst Lance X!”
Its mouth moved as if trying to say something, but I activated Burst Lance, engulfing it in an explosion. Just like last time, all that remained was the massive corpse of a fox.
“Hahahaha! No matter how much you pigs level up, it’s all meaningless!”
I taunted them with disdain. This was the punishment for making Father and the others suffer—again and again.
“Bu… Bubu!”
A pig dressed in a maid outfit was crawling toward Takt. It seems they still believe that if they can just cure Takt’s status ailments, they can win. How pointless.
There are more important matters to deal with than these pigs. I’ll leave their cannibalistic infighting to the Pig King.
That said, there’s something I absolutely need to confirm. I repeatedly jab my weapon into the lifeless body of the dragon, which appears to be undergoing post-mortem convulsions.
“Is it really dead?”
“Um… Motoyasu…?”
“What are you doing?”

Ren and Itsuki, who had been using status ailment attacks to ensure that Takt’s remaining pigs didn’t escape, cautiously asked me. What am I doing? This is an important precaution based on past experience.
“This thing turned into an Ōryū in the previous loop. If it were to transform here, we’d be repeating the same tragedy as last time. That’s why I’m making sure! Brionac X!”

I delivered an additional strike to the dragon’s corpse, ensuring that it was well and truly dead. With this, I’ve avoided the same outcome as last time. Back then, Father warned me about this in particular.
“Ah, right. There was an Ōryū among the Dragon Emperors that went on a rampage last time, wasn’t there?”
“Even though we essentially defeated it, it kept reviving over and over. That’s why I had to confirm that I truly finished it off.”
When we killed it in Siltvelt, it didn’t move at all, but you never know when it might cause trouble again. Even now, there’s still a lingering worry that it could transform regardless.
“Time to get rid of those worries—it’s Gaelion’s mealtime, na~!”
With a flutter, Rival—who hadn’t done a thing—descended onto the dragon’s corpse. Then, with loud crunching sounds, it burrowed its way inside.
“Ugh…”
“That’s pretty gruesome.”
Ren and Itsuki were watching the scene unfold. Father, having lowered his guard, was scanning the area just in case.
“King of Faubrey, I assume you’ve already taken precautions to prevent any unnecessary commotion when informing Takt’s subordinates?”
“Buhuhuhu… Of course. After all, there’s a fun time ahead.”
Disgusting. He was drooling.
“Still, this was quite the entertaining spectacle. I am satisfied.”
“R-Right… That’s… good to hear…”
Father seemed at a loss for words. Hey, Pig King, I don’t care if you’re the ruler of Faubrey—if you trouble Father any further, I’ll make you end up like Takt’s dragon.
“Haha, there’s nothing for the Four Holy Heroes to worry about. This so-called ‘hero’ and his band of criminals—I will personally see to their punishment.”
“Uh… R-Right. Please, just make sure this doesn’t lead to a world war…”
“Buhuhuhu… Of course. Leave it to me.”

And so, by the end of that day, Takt and his followers had their levels reset to 1. Ah, as for the companions Takt had left behind to hold the fort, they were instructed to celebrate his return. However, they were all taken out in one fell swoop with sleeping drugs that had been prepared for them. They had been so focused on trapping us that they completely failed to guard against threats in their own ranks. Apparently, further arrangements were being made behind the scenes, but for now, this was all the information we had access to.

“Then let it be proclaimed! Criminal Takt Alsahorn Faubrey! The Alsahorn household is hereby abolished! Strip them of all power, wealth, and influence, and punish every individual associated with him!”
The Pig King joyfully declared his verdict. Did he really enjoy this that much?
“King of Faubrey!”
One of his stunned vassals finally regained his composure and spoke up.
“Takt possesses the ability to wield multiple Hero weapons! In this apocalyptic era, he is a miracle unlike any other. For the sake of the world, could you not grant him clemency?”
